Milnes-rationality-conjecture-for-abelia.summary: Shows that certain "shadow" geometric quantities on abelian varieties (higher-dimensional doughnut-like shapes defined by equations) are honest rational numbers no matter which measuring tool (cohomology theory) you use, confirming a conjecture of James Milne.

Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from.summary: Settles a special case of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, but not the full conjecture. The conjecture links the rational points of an elliptic curve to its L-function. This paper proves its exact formula for curves of rank 0 or 1 (strictly, Selmer corank 0 or 1 at some prime). The prize problem asks about curves of every rank. For ranks 0 and 1, the rank part was already known from Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin; the new step is the exact formula at every odd prime.

The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-.summary: If a standard algebraic "upper bound" on an elliptic curve's rank says the rank is 0 or 1, then the true rank is exactly that. As an application, settles which primes of certain forms are sums of two rational cubes.

The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-fo.summary: Proves the part of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula that concerns powers of 2, for elliptic curves of rank 0 or 1, and shows it holds for almost all "twisted" versions of any given curve.

The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-3.summary: Proves that the Riemann zeta function and all Dirichlet L-functions have no zeros with real part above 7/8. This is a weak but unprecedented version of the Riemann Hypothesis, which predicts no zeros beyond real part 1/2.

The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-October-5-2.summary: An independent proof of a slightly weaker zero-free region (real part above 11/12) for the zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions, which already rules out the notorious "Siegel zeros".

Uniform-exclusion-of-Landau-Siegel-zeros.summary: Rules out "Landau–Siegel zeros", hypothetical bad zeros of L-functions very close to 1 that have haunted analytic number theory for nearly a century and block many results about primes.

Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational.summary: Shows that no computer program can decide, in general, whether a polynomial equation with integer coefficients has a solution in fractions. This settles the rational-number version of Hilbert's tenth problem, open since Matiyasevich solved the integer version in 1970.

A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curv.summary: For elliptic curves that have a rational point of order two, shows that a 2-adic algebraic rank estimate of 0 or 1 is always exact, a step towards the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.

Catalans-constant-is-irrational-Septembe.summary: Proves that Catalan's constant (1 − 1/9 + 1/25 − 1/49 + …) cannot be written as a fraction, a famous open problem on the same level as the irrationality of ζ(3).

Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-an.summary: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture: among all "twists" of a given elliptic curve, exactly half have rank 0 and half have rank 1 (in density), so higher ranks are rare.

The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twis.summary: Shows that the average rank of the twists of any elliptic curve tends to exactly 1/2, confirming Goldfeld's mean-rank prediction.

Ordinary-two-point-correlations-of-multi.summary: Proves the two-point Chowla conjecture: whether n has an even or odd number of prime factors is statistically independent of the same property for n+h. This is a central randomness statement about the primes.

The-Deligne-Drinfeld-conjecture-Septembe.summary: Proves the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture, describing exactly the building blocks of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, a symmetry object linking number theory, knot theory and quantum groups.

Reconstruction-of-Function-Fields-from-M.summary: Shows that a field of functions on a surface (or higher-dimensional variety) can be completely rebuilt from a small amount of algebraic "K-theory" data taken modulo a prime ℓ.

Reconstruction-from-Milnor-K-theory-modu.summary: In characteristic p, shows that a function field is determined by its first K-group modulo p together with how products of elements behave, via an elementary geometric reconstruction.

The-Bogomolov-Pop-reconstruction-theorem.summary: Proves the Bogomolov–Pop conjecture: a function field of dimension at least two is determined by a small quotient of its Galois group, a key goal of "anabelian geometry".

Unrestricted-pro-modularity-at-the-prime.summary: Shows that every suitable 2-dimensional 2-adic symmetry pattern (Galois representation) of the rationals appears in a space of modular forms, removing technical restrictions that held back earlier results at the prime 2.

The-Dimension-of-the-Two-Adic-Hecke-Alge.summary: Computes the size (Krull dimension four) of every component of the 2-adic Hecke algebra at odd level, settling the p=2 case of Emerton's dimension conjecture.

Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2.summary: Proves the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture at the prime 2 for odd two-dimensional representations: every "geometric-looking" Galois representation really comes from a modular form.

Weighted-Dilation-Graphs-Smooth-Shifted-.summary: Proves an Erdős conjecture that some numbers are hit by Euler's totient function almost as many times as possible (n^(1−ε) times). Also finds many primes p for which p−1 has only small prime factors.

The-Poisson-Dirichlet-Law-for-Prime-Pred.summary: Shows the prime factors of p−1, for a random prime p, are distributed like the pieces of a randomly broken stick (the Poisson–Dirichlet law), confirming a conjecture of Ford, Konyagin and Luca.

Prime-Predecessors-with-an-Even-Number-o.summary: Proves there are infinitely many primes p for which p−1 is squarefree with an even number of prime factors.

The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-in.summary: Proves the largest prime factors of n and n+1 behave independently. As a consequence, P(n) < P(n+1) holds for exactly half of all integers, settling an Erdős–Pomerance conjecture.

the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-pr.summary: Shows the primes cannot be written as a sumset A+B of two sets with at least two elements each, even after changing finitely many elements. This settles Ostmann's "inverse Goldbach" conjecture.

Global-Arthur-Enhancements-of-Cuspidal-E.summary: Technical companion in the geometric Langlands programme: builds "Arthur parameters" for automorphic data over function fields, assuming a decomposition proved elsewhere.

Rationality-of-the-Canonical-Unramified-.summary: Shows a natural filtration on automorphic functions over function fields is defined over the rational numbers, proving a rationality conjecture of Gaitsgory–Lafforgue–Raskin.

Ramanujan-Arthur-Decompositions-of-Cuspi.summary: Splits spaces of automorphic functions over function fields into pieces labelled by nilpotent orbits, a structural step towards the Ramanujan and Arthur conjectures.

Temperedness-at-ramified-places-for-glob.summary: Proves the generalized Ramanujan conjecture (local components are "tempered", i.e. as well-behaved as possible) for generic automorphic forms on exceptional groups over function fields.

The-Restricted-Geometric-Langlands-Equiv.summary: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for curves in positive characteristic, extending the recent landmark characteristic-zero proof to a new setting under some characteristic assumptions.

Constructible-tame-Hecke-eigensheaves-in.summary: Constructs Hecke eigensheaves, the geometric counterparts of automorphic forms, with tame ramification at a marked point on curves over finite fields.

Tame-Hecke-Eigensheaves-with-Several-Mar.summary: Extends the construction of tame Hecke eigensheaves for SL_n to curves with several marked points.

Frobenius-Structures-on-Tame-Hecke-Eigen.summary: Adds Frobenius (arithmetic) structure to the tame Hecke eigensheaves, linking the geometric constructions back to functions over finite fields.

Equidistribution-of-Prime-Degree-Torus-P.summary: Shows that certain lattice "packets" coming from number fields of prime degree become uniformly spread out as the discriminant grows, a higher-dimensional version of Duke's theorem.

Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Quartic-To.summary: Equidistribution of torus packets for quartic number fields with no intermediate field, for any order, combining measure rigidity with a cubic resolvent argument.

Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Sextic-Tor.summary: Equidistribution of ideal-class packets for primitive sextic number fields in the space of lattices.

The-Abelian-Zilber-Pink-Conjecture-Septe.summary: Proves the Zilber–Pink conjecture for abelian varieties: a subvariety contains only finitely many maximal "unexpectedly special" pieces. This is a broad finiteness principle for special points and subvarieties.

The-E-times-CM-Component-of-Zilber-Pink-.summary: One of three pieces of Zilber–Pink for curves in the moduli space of abelian surfaces: only finitely many points split as an elliptic curve times a CM elliptic curve.

Quaternionic-Division-Points-on-Curves-i.summary: Another piece of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂: only finitely many points have quaternionic multiplication.

Elliptic-Squares-and-Zilber-Pink-for-Cur.summary: Final piece: finitely many points isogenous to the square of an elliptic curve, completing the full Zilber–Pink conjecture for curves in the Siegel threefold.

The-irrationality-exponent-of-pi-is-2-Se.summary: Proves π cannot be approximated by fractions much better than a typical number, i.e. its irrationality exponent is exactly 2. As a bonus, the famous Flint–Hills series ∑1/(n³ sin² n) converges.

The-Margulis-Platonov-conjecture-over-gl.summary: Proves the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over function fields (including characteristic two), classifying normal subgroups of arithmetic groups.

The-Margulis-Platonov-conjecture-over-nu.summary: Proves the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over number fields: every normal subgroup of the rational points of a simple algebraic group is explained by local data.

Etale-covers-with-a-prescribed-exterior-.summary: Technical tool: constructs covering spaces of p-adic curves with a prescribed sheet over the outside of a few small disks, used for the p-adic section conjecture.

The-p-adic-section-conjecture-October-6-.summary: Proves the local p-adic version of Grothendieck's section conjecture: points on a curve correspond exactly to splittings of its fundamental group. Also gives the global conjecture for modular curves.

Squarefree-values-of-quartics-and-power-.summary: Proves that irreducible quartic polynomials take squarefree values as often as predicted. Quartics were the first open degree; also handles higher degrees up to 8.

A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-functi.summary: Answers Jacobsthal's question: any run of roughly k² consecutive integers contains a number coprime to any given number with k prime factors, removing a long-standing log factor.

The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-.summary: Proves the inhomogeneous (shifted) version of the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture about how well almost every real number can be approximated by fractions.

An-unconditional-first-moment-for-cubic-.summary: Proves Patterson's prediction for the average size of cubic Gauss sums over primes, unconditionally.

An-asymptotic-formula-for-the-number-of-.summary: Gives an asymptotic formula for how many distinct values Euler's totient function takes below x, answering a scaling question of Erdős and Hall.

Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-20.summary: Proves an Erdős conjecture: any fraction a/b can be written as a sum of about log log b distinct unit fractions (1/n), which is best possible.

Positive-lower-density-of-large-prime-ga.summary: Shows that a positive proportion of gaps between consecutive primes are larger than any fixed multiple of the average gap, answering a question of Erdős and Prachar.

Integral-points-on-character-varieties-o.summary: Shows integral points are dense on character varieties of curves (spaces of matrix representations of a curve's loops), answering Litt's question in the determinant-one case.

Bounded-Step-Walks-on-Gaussian-Primes-Se.summary: Proves the Gaussian moat conjecture: you cannot walk to infinity on Gaussian primes using steps of bounded length.

Primitive-roots-for-every-admissible-int.summary: Proves Artin's primitive root conjecture (in its infinitude form): every integer other than −1 or a perfect square is a primitive root for infinitely many primes. Previously only known conditionally on the Riemann Hypothesis.

Simultaneous-primitive-roots-a-condition.summary: Conditional extension: assuming inputs from the companion paper, many primes have several prescribed primes simultaneously as primitive roots.

Modularity-of-elliptic-curves-over-imagi.summary: Proves that every elliptic curve over an imaginary quadratic field is modular, extending the celebrated Wiles-type modularity theorem for rational elliptic curves.

Open-Homomorphisms-of-Global-Solvably-Cl.summary: Proves Uchida's conjecture: open maps between solvably closed Galois groups of number fields always come from field embeddings.

The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abe.summary: Settles the Hodge conjecture, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, for one important family of spaces but not in general: abelian varieties with complex multiplication, which have unusually many symmetries. On these, every "Hodge class" (a shape seen by topology) comes from actual algebraic subvarieties. Through known implications, this also gives the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields and Grothendieck’s Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties.

Algebraic-Kuga-Satake-correspondences-an.summary: Proves the Hodge conjecture for all powers of K3 surfaces whose lattice fits a specific shape.

Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelia.summary: Proves the Hodge conjecture for powers of certain abelian sixfolds and all abelian varieties of dimension at most five with an imaginary-quadratic action.

Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-.summary: Proves the Hodge conjecture (that certain topological "shadows" always come from real geometric subvarieties) for all powers of Jacobians attached to generic covers of curves.

A-Conditional-Reduction-for-Algebraic-Ku.summary: A conditional reduction: a single algebraic correspondence of a certain kind would be enough to produce the full Kuga–Satake correspondence.

Orbifold-and-logarithmic-Iitaka-subaddit.summary: Proves Campana's orbifold version of Iitaka's subadditivity conjecture: the "complexity" of a fibred space is at least the sum of the complexities of the base and fibre.

Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-.summary: Proves Popa's logarithmic variation inequality, measuring how a family's complexity grows with how much the fibres vary.

The-reverse-logarithmic-Kodaira-inequali.summary: Proves a reverse log Kodaira inequality, giving additivity of the log Kodaira dimension for smooth families.

Projective-Hodge-lines-and-ordinary-Iita.summary: Proves Iitaka's subadditivity conjecture κ(X) ≥ κ(F) + κ(Z) in characteristic zero, a central open problem in the classification of algebraic varieties since the 1970s.

B-semiampleness-for-compact-log-smooth-K.summary: A technical step in classifying compact Kähler manifolds: shows the "boundary" part of a nicely behaved fibration is eventually generated by its sections (b-semiampleness).

Log-abundance-for-compact-Kahler-spaces-.summary: Assuming log Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance for compact Kähler spaces in all dimensions.

Uniform-indices-for-semi-log-canonical-l.summary: Shows a uniform index for semi-log-canonical Calabi–Yau pairs: one fixed multiple of the canonical divisor is trivial, depending only on dimension and coefficients.

Conditional-good-minimal-models-for-comp.summary: Conditional existence of good minimal models for compact Kähler fourfolds, assuming several conjectures.

Log-abundance-in-characteristic-zero-Sep.summary: Proves the log abundance conjecture in all dimensions over characteristic zero, one of the two main open conjectures of the minimal model program. Also gives nonvanishing for the canonical bundle.

Minimal-metrics-and-interior-injectivity.summary: Technical: shows that minimal metrics on nef adjoint bundles have no singularities (zero Lelong numbers) and proves an injectivity theorem.

Fourfold-nonvanishing-by-minimal-metrics.summary: Proves the nonvanishing conjecture for fourfolds: if the canonical bundle is pseudo-effective, some multiple has a section.

Lifting-sections-from-the-reduced-suppor.summary: Technical step: lifting sections from the boundary gives log abundance once nonvanishing is known in dimension ≤ 4.

Schnell-fiber-spaces-and-good-canonical-.summary: Proves the Campana–Peternell inequality κ(X) ≥ κ(D) under a pseudo-effectivity hypothesis.

Uniform-log-Iitaka-fibrations-and-bounde.summary: Uniform effective log Iitaka fibrations in dimension ≥ 5: one fixed multiple of the log canonical divisor always defines the Iitaka fibration.

Uniform-Pluricanonical-Iitaka-Fibrations.summary: Proves the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture: in each dimension, one fixed pluricanonical degree works for every variety.

Relative-denominators-and-effective-syst.summary: Shows that certain fibrations of balanced (log Calabi–Yau) spaces up to dimension four have uniformly bounded "denominators", a finiteness statement used in classification theory.

Arithmetic-Stein-degree-bounds-for-log-C.summary: Bounds field extension degrees of boundary components of log Calabi–Yau pairs over arbitrary characteristic-zero fields.

Uniform-effective-log-Iitaka-fibrations-.summary: Proves the effective log Iitaka conjecture for 4-dimensional spaces: one fixed multiple of the canonical divisor always reveals the variety's natural fibration.

Abundance-after-nonvanishing-for-compact.summary: For compact Kähler fourfolds, shows that once one section of the adjoint bundle exists, abundance follows: the bundle is generated by its sections.

Log-abundance-in-numerical-dimension-one.summary: Proves abundance in numerical dimension one for log canonical threefolds in characteristic p > 3.

Abundance-in-numerical-dimension-one-for.summary: The terminal-threefold special case of abundance in numerical dimension one in characteristic p > 3.

Numerical-semiampleness-of-nef-adjoint-c.summary: Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds, a Kähler analogue of generalised abundance.

Numerical-Semiampleness-of-Nef-Adjoint-D.summary: Proves the Generalised Abundance Conjecture: nef adjoint divisors with a nef twist are numerically semiample.

Minimal-models-and-Mori-fibre-spaces-for.summary: Proves existence of minimal models or Mori fibre spaces for all generalized log canonical pairs in characteristic zero.

Minimal-models-in-numerical-dimension-on.summary: Existence of minimal models for varieties whose canonical bundle has numerical dimension one.

The-ordinary-double-point-gap-in-every-d.summary: Proves the ordinary-double-point gap conjecture: singular klt points have normalized volume at most 2(n−1)^n, with equality only for the simplest singularity.

The-normalized-volume-gap-in-dimension-f.summary: Proves in dimension four that the simplest kind of singular point (an ordinary double point) is the "least singular" possible, as measured by normalized volume.

Fujitas-freeness-conjecture-September-23.summary: Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture: K_X + mL is globally generated for m ≥ dim X + 1. This classic 1985 conjecture was previously known only in low dimensions.

Nagatas-Conjecture-for-Plane-Curves-Sept.summary: Proves Nagata's 1959 conjecture: a plane curve through r ≥ 10 general points with given multiplicities must have high degree. This was a famous open problem in algebraic geometry.

Maximal-Seshadri-Constants-on-Arbitrary-.summary: Multipoint Seshadri constants on any surface are maximal for many points, settling the Nagata–Biran conjecture for surfaces.

Maximal-Multipoint-Seshadri-Constants-in.summary: Shows that, for many general points on a higher-dimensional variety, a measure of local positivity (the Seshadri constant) is as large as volume allows.

Maximal-multipoint-Seshadri-constants-in.summary: The positive-characteristic version: Seshadri constants at many general points are maximal, also over fields like finite fields.

Blochs-Conjecture-for-Surfaces-with-pg-e.summary: Proves Bloch's conjecture: for complex surfaces with no holomorphic 2-forms, zero-cycles are controlled by the Albanese variety. Open since 1975.

Projective-Space-Bases-of-Lagrangian-Fib.summary: Shows that whenever a hyperkähler manifold (a highly symmetric higher-dimensional cousin of the K3 surface) is fibred by Lagrangian tori, the base of the fibration is always ordinary projective space.

The-Strong-Hyperkahler-SYZ-Conjecture-Se.summary: Proves the strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture: a line bundle that "looks like" it should come from a torus fibration really does, so such fibrations exist whenever predicted.

Every-complex-K3-surface-is-Oka-Septembe.summary: Proves every K3 surface is "Oka", meaning maps into it are as flexible as maps into ordinary complex space. This settles a conjecture in the field linking complex analysis and geometry.

P-equals-W-in-composite-rank-for-fixed-d.summary: Completes the P = W conjecture (fixed determinant) in every coprime rank, matching two very different natural filtrations on the cohomology of Higgs moduli spaces and character varieties.

The-equivariant-cohomological-Hikita-con.summary: Proves the equivariant Hikita conjecture for all quivers, linking the cohomology of one symplectic space to the functions on its "mirror" (the Coulomb branch).

A-projective-fourfold-with-large-fundame.summary: Disproves Shafarevich's holomorphic convexity conjecture even for varieties with large fundamental group, via an explicit fourfold whose universal cover is not Stein.

A-surface-counterexample-to-Shafarevich-.summary: Gives a complex surface whose universal cover is not holomorphically convex, disproving Shafarevich's conjecture already in dimension two.

An-explicit-failure-of-complex-affine-sp.summary: Disproves Zariski's cancellation problem over the complex numbers: there is a 4-dimensional space X that is not ordinary 4-space, yet X times a line is ordinary 5-space. This was a famous open problem in affine algebraic geometry.

A-singular-normal-affine-surface-with-fr.summary: Builds a singular surface whose tangent sheaf is free, disproving the Lipman–Zariski conjecture that a free tangent sheaf forces smoothness.

A-stable-coordinate-that-is-not-a-coordi.summary: An explicit degree-5 polynomial in four variables that is not a "coordinate" but becomes one after adding a variable, disproving the stable coordinate and Abhyankar–Sathaye conjectures.

An-explicit-noncoordinate-polynomial-wit.summary: An explicit noncoordinate polynomial in four variables whose zero set is still a copy of 3-space, disproving the Abhyankar–Sathaye embedding conjecture.

ample-rank-two-bundles-on-the-quadric-su.summary: Disproves Griffiths' 1969 conjecture that algebraically positive (ample) vector bundles always admit metrics of positive curvature, with rank-two examples on P¹×P¹.

Canonical-ampleness-of-compact-hyperboli.summary: Proves Kobayashi's conjecture: a compact Kähler manifold with no entire curves (complex lines) in it has ample canonical bundle, so is algebraic.

Universal-cover-splitting-for-compact-Ka.summary: If a compact Kähler manifold's tangent bundle splits into two integrable pieces, its universal cover splits as a product (two-summand Beauville conjecture).

Integrability-of-split-tangent-bundles-o.summary: On rationally connected manifolds, any splitting of the tangent bundle into two pieces is automatically integrable, proving Höring's conjecture.

A-high-arity-counterexample-to-Pixton-co.summary: Disproves Pixton's original completeness conjecture for tautological relations on moduli spaces of curves, using an enormous example (genus 10^60).

Irrational-cubic-fourfolds-with-geometri.summary: Shows some cubic fourfolds with an associated K3 surface are still irrational, disproving Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture, a central prediction about which cubic fourfolds are rational.

A-Gepner-stability-condition-on-every-sm.summary: Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture: every quintic threefold has a stability condition with a predicted symmetry coming from string theory (Gepner point).

Prescribed-large-volume-charges-on-three.summary: Constructs Bridgeland stability conditions near the "large volume limit" on all Calabi–Yau threefolds, a long-sought existence result.

Termination-of-generalized-log-canonical.summary: Shows the minimal model program (a step-by-step simplification of a geometric space) always stops after finitely many steps for compact Kähler fourfolds of a general type.

Termination-of-generalized-canonical-fli.summary: Termination of generalized canonical flips for compact Kähler fourfolds (companion variant).

Termination-for-projective-log-canonical.summary: Proves termination of every minimal model program for log canonical fourfolds in characteristic zero, a key open case of the termination conjecture.

Finite-ordinary-minimal-model-programs-o.summary: Shows every run of the minimal model program on a compact Kähler klt fourfold terminates, ending at a simplified model (a companion version of the termination result).
Shows a finite run of the minimal model program exists for compact Kähler klt fourfolds, ending at a simplified model (a companion version of the termination result).

The-abelianity-conjecture-for-special-co.summary: Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: "special" compact Kähler manifolds (those with no map onto a general-type orbifold) have essentially abelian fundamental groups.

Two-step-monodromy-of-special-quasi-proj.summary: Independent proof that linear representations of fundamental groups of special quasi-projective varieties are nearly 2-step nilpotent.

A-conditional-abelianity-theorem-for-spe.summary: Assuming related results, shows a specific kind of 4-dimensional orbifold has a nearly abelian fundamental group (its loops essentially commute).

Semialgebraic-universal-covers-of-normal.summary: Proves the Kollár–Pardon conjecture classifying when universal covers of projective varieties are semialgebraic: exactly products of symmetric domains, affine spaces and compact pieces.

Symmetry-of-semialgebraic-bounded-domain.summary: Bounded semialgebraic domains with compact quotients are symmetric domains, answering a Kollár–Pardon question.

Ambiently-homeomorphic-isolated-hypersur.summary: Disproves Zariski's 1971 multiplicity conjecture: two hypersurface singularities can be topologically identical yet have different multiplicities.
Gives two singular hypersurfaces in four complex variables that look identical topologically but have different multiplicities, answering Zariski's question already in this low dimension.

Global-Spherical-Shells-on-Minimal-Surfa.summary: Proves the Global Spherical Shell conjecture, which completes the classification of a mysterious class (VII) of compact complex surfaces: the last major gap in the Kodaira classification of surfaces.

Contact-Fano-manifolds-and-the-LeBrun-Sa.summary: Proves the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture (positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds are symmetric) and classifies contact Fano manifolds, a decades-old problem bridging Riemannian and algebraic geometry.

The-Generalized-Mukai-Conjecture-Septemb.summary: Proves the generalized Mukai conjecture bounding the Picard number of Fano manifolds in terms of the minimal degree of rational curves.

Topological-triviality-of-mu-constant-fa.summary: Shows families of surface singularities with constant Milnor number are topologically trivial, resolving the surface case of the famous μ-constant problem (Lê–Ramanujam).

Virasoro-Constraints-under-Projectivizat.summary: Virasoro constraints (symmetries of curve-counting invariants) pass from a variety to any projective bundle over it.

Virasoro-Constraints-for-Projective-Comp.summary: Proves the Virasoro conjecture for curve counts on all smooth complete intersections in projective space.

Bounded-klt-complements-for-Fano-contrac.summary: Proves Shokurov's bounded klt complements conjecture for Fano contractions with finitely many coefficients.

Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-c.summary: Proves a Birkar–Shokurov conjecture: near any point of a Fano-type fibration one can find a divisor whose singularities are controlled by dimension alone.

The-Campana-Peternell-conjecture-in-dime.summary: Proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six: Fano sixfolds with nef tangent bundle are homogeneous.

Anticanonical-nonvanishing-from-smooth-s.summary: Shows that if the anticanonical bundle carries a smooth semipositive metric, then some power has a section, in every dimension.

Invariant-anticanonical-indices-and-conv.summary: Technical step on torus-invariant anticanonical indices used for anticanonical nonvanishing.

Bounded-anticanonical-metrics-on-klt-pai.summary: Technical step: bounded semipositive metrics imply anticanonical sections under an Euler characteristic condition.

Cohomological-transfer-and-equivariant-a.summary: Technical step: converting invariant twisted sections into genuine anticanonical sections.

Metric-descent-and-rank-preserving-contr.summary: A technical step: transfers a semipositive curvature condition on the anticanonical bundle from a variety down to the base of a fibration.

Integrable-metrics-and-effectivity-with-.summary: A technical step: shows curvature-controlled metrics force divisors to be effective up to a controlled boundary correction.

Exact-orders-and-invariant-anticanonical.summary: A technical step: realizes an asymptotic order of vanishing by an actual effective anticanonical divisor.

Global-quantum-geometric-Langlands-at-ir.summary: Proves the quantum geometric Langlands equivalence at irrational level for every simple group and curve, a deformation of the recently proved geometric Langlands conjecture.

Removable-Boundaries-and-Rigidity-of-Cir.summary: Shows circle domains with removable boundary are conformally rigid, one direction of the He–Schramm conjecture.

Koebes-Circle-Domain-Conjecture-Septembe.summary: Proves Koebe's 1908 conjecture: any planar domain, however many holes, can be conformally mapped to one whose holes are round disks or points.

Brennans-conjecture-and-sharp-inverse-sq.summary: Proves Brennan's conjecture on how wildly the derivative of a conformal map can blow up, a central problem in geometric function theory since 1978.

A-strict-inverse-first-power-bound-for-u.summary: Disproves Kraetzer's conjectured formula for the integral means spectrum of bounded univalent functions at one parameter.

The-Falconer-distance-conjecture-in-all-.summary: Proves the Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions: any set of dimension over d/2 determines a positive-length set of distances. A flagship problem in harmonic analysis.

The-Kakeya-maximal-conjecture-in-three-d.summary: Proves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in 3D, the strong quantitative form of the statement that sets containing a needle in every direction can't be small.

Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-fu.summary: Proves that in 4D any set containing a unit segment in every direction has full dimension (the Kakeya conjecture in four dimensions).

Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in.summary: Proves Fourier series of every L log L function converge almost everywhere, a classical question near the boundary of Carleson's theorem and Kolmogorov's counterexample.

Ultraflat-real-Littlewood-polynomials-Oc.summary: Constructs polynomials with ±1 coefficients whose size is nearly constant on the unit circle ("ultraflat"), answering a classical question of Littlewood for real coefficients.

Nearly-minimal-maxima-and-positive-minim.summary: Littlewood polynomials with modulus bounded above and below on the whole circle, a preliminary flatness result.

Asymptotically-minimal-maxima-of-real-Li.summary: Shows ±1 polynomials can have maximum modulus close to √N, disproving an Erdős-type conjecture and Turyn's conjecture that binary merit factors are bounded.

Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourie.summary: Proves the Fourier restriction conjecture for the sphere in 3D for bounded data, a central open problem in harmonic analysis.

Diagonal-Fourier-extension-for-positivel.summary: Proves the restriction (Fourier extension) conjecture for positively curved surfaces in 3D, with consequences for Schrödinger equations.

Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimen.summary: Proves the Bochner–Riesz conjecture in three dimensions, describing exactly when smoothed Fourier inversion on balls converges in L^p.

Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-d.summary: Proves Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the 3D wave equation: waves average out to become smoother than their initial data.

Endpoint-convergence-for-the-planar-Schr.summary: Resolves the endpoint of Carleson's convergence problem in 2D: solutions of the Schrödinger equation converge pointwise to their initial data for H^{1/3} data.

Endpoint-pointwise-convergence-for-the-S.summary: The sharp endpoint for pointwise convergence of the Schrödinger equation in every dimension ≥ 3.

Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiabil.summary: Proves the David–Semmes conjecture in higher codimension: bounded Riesz transforms force a measure to be uniformly rectifiable (built from nice pieces).

Annular-variation-of-the-triangular-Hilb.summary: Proves bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric L³ point, a notoriously hard multilinear singular integral.

An-L3-bound-for-the-dyadic-triangular-Hi.summary: Proves a bound for a simplified (dyadic) model of the triangular Hilbert transform, a notoriously hard averaging operator in harmonic analysis.

The-maximal-triangular-Hilbert-transform.summary: Maximal bound for the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point, giving almost-everywhere convergence.

A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for.summary: Proves Stein's conjecture (at the short scale) on Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz vector fields, a famous problem related to Zygmund's conjecture.

The-geometric-case-of-the-Erdos-similari.summary: Resolves the geometric-sequence case of the Erdős similarity conjecture: large sets can avoid every scaled copy of {qⁿ}.

The-dyadic-case-of-the-Erdos-similarity-.summary: Constructs large sets of real numbers that contain no scaled and shifted copy of the sequence 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, …, settling this case of the Erdős similarity conjecture.

An-Endpoint-Gradient-Bound-for-the-Cente.summary: Proves the gradient of the centered disk maximal function is controlled in L¹, resolving the planar case of the Hajłasz–Onninen problem.

An-L3-bound-for-the-trilinear-Hilbert-tr.summary: Proves an L³ bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform, an operator long believed out of reach of current techniques.

The-symmetric-Mahler-conjecture-and-its-.summary: Proves the symmetric Mahler conjecture: among symmetric convex bodies, the product of volume and dual volume is minimized by cubes (and Hanner polytopes). Open since 1939.

The-Mahler-Conjecture-for-General-Convex.summary: Proves the general Mahler conjecture: simplices minimize the volume product among all convex bodies.

Symplectic-Balls-in-Symmetric-Polar-Prod.summary: Computes the symplectic width of K × K° as 4, giving a symplectic proof of the symmetric Mahler conjecture (Viterbo's approach).

Pettys-projection-volume-conjecture-in-d.summary: Proves Petty's projection conjecture in dimensions ≥ 4: ellipsoids minimize projection-body volume.

A-product-counterexample-to-the-simplex-.summary: A product of two simplices beats Brannen's conjectured maximizer for projection-body volume.

Planar-Graph-Metrics-Embed-into-L1-with-.summary: Proves the planar embedding conjecture: distances in planar graphs embed in L₁ with constant distortion, implying constant flow-cut gaps.

L1-Embeddings-of-Graphs-of-Bounded-Treew.summary: Bounded-treewidth graphs embed into L₁ with bounded distortion (GNRS conjecture for bounded treewidth).

An-atomic-certificate-for-triangular-lat.summary: An atomic certificate proving the triangular lattice is universally optimal among planar configurations.

Universal-optimality-of-the-triangular-l.summary: Proves the triangular lattice universally minimizes energy for a large class of potentials, the 2D analogue of the Cohn–Kumar–Miller–Radchenko–Viazovska theorem.

A-sharp-Fourier-certificate-for-planar-c.summary: Proves the Cohn–Elkies linear programming bound is sharp in the plane, giving a Fourier-analytic proof of hexagonal circle packing optimality.

Triangular-minimality-for-planar-Coulomb.summary: Proves the Sandier–Serfaty conjecture: the triangular lattice minimizes Coulomb renormalized energy (relevant to vortices in superconductors).

The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjectu.summary: Proves the log Brunn–Minkowski conjecture for symmetric convex bodies, a major strengthening of the Brunn–Minkowski inequality.

A-single-lattice-covering-bound-of-order.summary: Shows every convex body in n dimensions can cover space by lattice translates with overlap density at most about n log n.

Translative-covering-densities-of-order-.summary: Shows n log n is the right order: some symmetric convex bodies need covering density at least c·n log n.

A-dimension-free-logarithmic-Sobolev-ine.summary: Shows a key inequality controlling how quickly random quantities concentrate holds without dependence on dimension, for well-behaved (subgaussian log-concave) distributions.

Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-.summary: Shows any n points in L_p can be squeezed into very few dimensions (n^{o(1)}) with bounded distortion, answering Naor's question for p ≠ 2 (where the classic Johnson–Lindenstrauss trick fails).

Hyperbolicity-Cones-Without-Semidefinite.summary: Disproves the generalized Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones cannot be described by semidefinite programming at all, even with extra variables.

A-Nonspectrahedral-Hyperbolicity-Cone-Se.summary: An explicit degree-16 polynomial in 23 variables whose hyperbolicity cone is not spectrahedral, disproving the geometric generalized Lax conjecture.

An-Exact-Semidefinite-Lift-of-a-Nonspect.summary: Shows the companion nonspectrahedral cone still has a semidefinite lift with extra variables, separating the two forms of the Lax conjecture.

The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Di.summary: Proves the Gaussian propeller conjecture: the best way to split Gaussian space to maximize total squared "centre of mass" is a three-bladed propeller. Gives tight hardness for kernel clustering.

The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem.summary: Proves vectors in the unit ball can be signed so every partial sum stays within C√d, determining the Euclidean Steinitz constant: a classical discrepancy question.

A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite.summary: Every infinite-dimensional Banach space contains a compact doubling set with no bi-Lipschitz embedding into finite dimensions, answering the Lang–Plaut problem.

Edit-Distance-in-l1-Matching-Bounds-up-t.summary: Pins down exactly (up to constants in the exponent) how much distortion is needed to embed edit distance into L₁, a central question in algorithmic metric embeddings.

Finite-Circle-Obstructions-Binary-Codes-.summary: Lower-bound constructions (via finite circles and binary codes) for embedding edit distance into L₁.

Tree-Constructions-for-the-l1-Distortion.summary: Alternative tree-based lower-bound constructions for L₁ distortion of binary edit distance.

Finite-angular-cylinder-covers-below-the.summary: Covers a tetrahedron by cylinders of total base area below half its smallest shadow, disproving Bang's half-area conjecture (related to the plank problem).

Finite-cylinder-approximation-of-ruled-s.summary: A technical tool: approximates families of line segments swept through space by finitely many cylinders, used in the cylinder-covering counterexample.

Slope-field-perturbations-of-the-two-cyl.summary: Alternative counterexample: perturbing the two-cylinder cover of a tetrahedron goes below half area.

Finite-triangular-approximation-of-radia.summary: Another way to cover a tetrahedron with thin cylinders of total area below half its shadow, via triangular approximations of radial sweeps.

A-sharp-entropy-bound-and-the-simplex-in.summary: Proves simplices maximize the isotropic constant among convex bodies, a sharp form of the slicing problem circle of ideas. Also proves a sharp entropy bound for log-concave densities.

The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-20.summary: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture, the most important open problem in hardness of approximation. It implies many known algorithms (e.g. Goemans–Williamson Max-Cut) are optimal.

A-Direct-Proof-of-Optimal-Max-Cut-Hardne.summary: Directly proves it is NP-hard to beat the Goemans–Williamson approximation ratio for Max-Cut.

The-Factor-Two-Hardness-Threshold-for-Ve.summary: Proves Vertex Cover is NP-hard to approximate within any factor below 2, so the trivial 2-approximation is optimal.

Constant-factor-hardness-of-Min-UnCut-Se.summary: Shows it is NP-hard to approximate the Min-UnCut graph partitioning problem within any constant factor.

Constant-factor-hardness-of-directed-fee.summary: Shows it is NP-hard to approximate, within any constant factor, the fewest vertices to delete to remove all directed cycles from a graph.

Exact-Derandomization-of-Logarithmic-Spa.summary: Proves L = BPL: any randomized algorithm using logarithmic memory can be made deterministic with the same memory. A flagship open problem in complexity theory.

Turn-Based-Stochastic-Mean-Payoff-Games-.summary: A quasipolynomial-time algorithm to solve stochastic mean-payoff games, two-player games with random moves and long-run average rewards.

Mean-payoff-parity-games-in-quasipolynom.summary: A quasipolynomial-time algorithm for mean-payoff parity games, which combine long-run reward with a winning condition used in program verification.

Deterministic-quasipolynomial-time-mean-.summary: Solves mean-payoff games in deterministic quasipolynomial time, a long-standing open problem near the NP ∩ coNP frontier.

Randomized-quasipolynomial-time-mean-pay.summary: A randomized quasipolynomial-time algorithm for mean-payoff games (precursor to the deterministic version).

Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-Se.summary: Proves Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness, a variant of Unique Games implying sharp coloring hardness.

Hardness-of-finding-large-independent-se.summary: Proves it is NP-hard to color a 3-colorable graph with any constant number of colors, a famous open problem since the 1970s.

Matrix-Multiplication-Nine-Fourths-Octob.summary: Proves matrix multiplication exponent ω ≤ 9/4 (2.25), a huge jump from the previous ~2.371. Multiplying n×n matrices would take about n^2.25 operations.

Complex-Matrix-Multiplication-Below-2.25.summary: Secondary writeup: ω < 2.258 and rectangular matrix multiplication bounds in characteristic zero.

Staggered-extraction-for-exact-matrix-mu.summary: A small improvement ω < 2.37105… valid over every field, including positive characteristic.

A-cubic-lower-bound-for-border-determina.summary: Proves the permanent needs determinants of size at least cubic to express it, improving the quadratic bound that stood since 2004 and advancing the algebraic P vs NP programme.

Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-Sep.summary: Multiplies n-bit integers faster than n log n on multitape Turing machines, disproving the Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture.

Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-.summary: Proves a polylog(k)-competitive randomized k-server algorithm on all metrics, settling the randomized k-server conjecture (in the O(log² k) form).

Uniform-computation-of-the-squared-logar.summary: Efficient implementation of the O(log² k) randomized k-server algorithm on finite metrics.

One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-.summary: Shows one sample per element suffices for constant-competitive matroid prophet inequalities, even against a very powerful adversary.

Beyond-the-Square-Root-Exponent-for-Dept.summary: Breaks the 2^{√n} barrier for depth-3 circuit lower bounds for an explicit function, a decades-old barrier in circuit complexity.

A-Fully-Polynomial-Randomized-Approximat.summary: Gives an efficient randomized algorithm to approximately count perfect matchings in any graph, a central open problem in counting complexity (bipartite case: Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda 2001).

Entropy-and-Face-Dimension-of-the-Perfec.summary: Proves the Anari–Oveis Gharan–Vinzant entropy conjecture for perfect matching distributions.

An-FPRAS-for-Common-Integer-Polymatroid-.summary: An efficient randomized algorithm to approximately count common integer bases of two polymatroids, a broad generalization of matroid counting.

Approximate-counting-of-common-bases-of-.summary: Efficient approximate counting of common bases of two matroids, a long-open counting problem.

Exact-Uniform-Sampling-of-Contingency-Ta.summary: Exact uniform sampling of contingency tables (integer matrices with given row/column sums) in expected polynomial time.

An-FPRAS-for-Cell-Bounded-Contingency-Ta.summary: An efficient algorithm to approximately count integer tables with prescribed row/column sums and per-cell limits (common in statistics).

Uniform-Matrix-Hitting-Points-in-Every-P.summary: Deterministic matrix substitutions detecting nonzero noncommutative formulas in every positive characteristic.

One-Rational-Matrix-Hitting-Point-for-No.summary: One rational matrix tuple that detects every nonzero noncommutative formula of given size (deterministic identity testing).

Polynomial-Hitting-Lists-for-Noncommutat.summary: Deterministically produces a short list of matrix inputs that can detect whether a noncommutative rational formula is nonzero.

Constant-factor-hardness-of-uniform-spar.summary: Shows it is NP-hard to approximate Uniform Sparsest Cut (finding the most "bottlenecked" split of a graph) within any constant factor.

Near-square-root-logarithmic-integrality.summary: Shows the standard semidefinite programming relaxation for sparsest cut can be off by nearly √log n, almost matching the famous ARV guarantee.

Additive-hardness-and-unbounded-configur.summary: Disproves the Modified Integer Round-Up Conjecture for bin packing: the LP relaxation can be off by an unbounded additive amount.

Sharp-binary-information-contraction-on-.summary: Proves the Courtade–Kumar "most informative Boolean function" conjecture: a dictator function retains the most information through a noisy channel.

Hellinger-contraction-with-arbitrary-Boo.summary: Proves the Hellinger conjecture: a sharp limit on how much a noisy Boolean function's output can lose information, for any output bias.

Almost-Linear-Time-Maximum-Cardinality-M.summary: Finds maximum matchings in general graphs in almost-linear time, extending recent max-flow breakthroughs to non-bipartite matching.

An-Almost-Linear-Approximation-Scheme-fo.summary: Approximates edit distance (minimum insertions, deletions, substitutions between strings) within 1+ε in almost-linear time.

Uniform-quasipolynomial-time-trace-recon.summary: Uniform quasipolynomial-time algorithm to reconstruct strings from randomly deleted copies.

A-latest-anchor-induction-with-spectrall.summary: An improved bound on how many randomly corrupted copies (with deletions) of a string suffice to reconstruct it.

quantitative-lower-bounds-for-trace-reco.summary: Proves trace reconstruction needs superpolynomially many samples, answering a central open question negatively.

A-polynomial-time-algorithm-for-three-ma.summary: Polynomial-time algorithm for scheduling unit jobs with precedence constraints on 3 machines, one of the original open problems in Garey–Johnson (1979).

Single-Exponential-Recovery-and-Bounded-.summary: Technical recovery algorithm used to reach the 1+2/e approximation threshold for k-median.

The-Approximation-Threshold-for-Metric-k.summary: Gives a (1+2/e+ε)-approximation for metric k-median, matching the known hardness; this settles the approximability of k-median.

Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shift.summary: Shows the perfect matching polytope has no small semidefinite description, answering Rothvoss's question.

Average-Sensitivity-of-Polynomial-Thresh.summary: Proves the Gotsman–Linial conjecture asymptotically: degree-d threshold functions have average sensitivity O(d√n).

A-Polynomial-Time-2-Approximation-for-Sh.summary: A 2-approximation for shortest common superstring, matching the long-conjectured greedy ratio.

An-exponential-state-lower-bound-for-two.summary: Shows flipping the answer of a two-way nondeterministic automaton (a simple machine reading input back and forth) can require exponentially more states.

An-exponential-two-way-deterministic-sta.summary: Resolves the Sakoda–Sipser conjecture over growing alphabets: two-way deterministic automata need exponentially more states than one-way nondeterministic ones.

An-explicit-power-saving-for-the-exact-d.summary: Computes the discrete Fourier transform with o(n log n) operations, beating the FFT's long-standing bound in an exact arithmetic model.

Finite-tensor-savings-and-exact-Fourier-.summary: Constructs exact linear circuits for Fourier transform of size o(n log n), refuting the conjectured Ω(n log n) lower bound in that model.

Polynomial-Mixing-of-the-Switch-Chain-fo.summary: Proves the switch Markov chain samples random graphs with given degrees in polynomial time, for every degree sequence (Kannan–Tetali–Vempala).

A-superquadratic-separation-between-sens.summary: Disproves the conjecture that block sensitivity is at most quadratic in sensitivity, sharpening the landscape after Huang's sensitivity theorem.

Parity-lifts-and-bounded-treewidth-witne.summary: Technical reductions encoding puzzles into the Weisfeiler–Leman graph comparison test, used to prove its hardness.

The-complexity-of-identifying-a-graph-by.summary: Deciding whether the Weisfeiler–Leman algorithm (a standard heuristic for graph isomorphism) uniquely identifies a graph is EXPTIME-complete.

Unconditional-time-lower-bounds-for-Weis.summary: Proves without unproved assumptions that the k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman graph test needs n^{Ω(k)} time.

Variable-dimension-Weisfeiler-Leman-equi.summary: Shows deciding Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence with the dimension as input is EXPTIME-complete, even for graphs of degree three.

Finite-Monoid-Computations-and-a-Uniform.summary: First proof that every regular language can be written with at most 13 nested "repeat" stars when complement is allowed.

Generalized-Star-Height-at-Most-Four-Sep.summary: Improves the uniform bound: every regular language needs at most 4 nested stars when complement is allowed.

Generalized-Star-Height-at-Most-Three-Se.summary: Shows every regular language has generalized star height at most 3, a strong uniform bound for the famous open generalized star-height problem.

Homogeneous-depth-five-lower-bounds-for-.summary: Sharp n^{Θ(√n)} lower bounds for homogeneous depth-5 circuits computing iterated matrix multiplication.

The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinea.summary: Proves the quasilinear PCP-for-PPAD conjecture, implying tight hardness for approximate Nash equilibria.

Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-P.summary: Simulates one-tape Turing machines running for T steps in about T^{2/5} space, improving the √T barrier.

Subset-Sum-in-Time-2-power-0-49n-October.summary: Solves Subset Sum in O(2^{0.49n}) time, the first improvement over the 1974 meet-in-the-middle 2^{n/2} algorithm.

A-Low-Space-Algorithm-for-Worst-Case-Sub.summary: Solves Subset Sum in the classical 2^{n/2} time using far less memory (2^{n/5}).

Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-.summary: Samples well-conditioned log-concave distributions with only d^ε gradient queries, showing dimension dependence can be nearly eliminated.

Memory-and-precision-in-noiseless-Gaussi.summary: One-pass learners with limited memory need Ω(d log(1/ε)) samples for noiseless Gaussian regression.

Posterior-replicas-and-conditional-infor.summary: An information-theoretic tool for proving that memory-limited learners need many samples for linear regression.

Localization-costs-and-information-growt.summary: Bounds how fast information accumulates for memory-limited learners from noiseless Gaussian measurements.

Projection-moments-positive-cap-dominati.summary: Alternative proofs that memory-limited learners need Ω(d log 1/ε) samples, via projection moment estimates on the sphere.

Replacing-Gaussian-observations-in-memor.summary: A replacement lemma for memory-constrained inference: swapping Gaussian observations changes information only slightly.

Subsphere-methods-for-memory-sample-lowe.summary: Subsphere method giving another proof of the memory–sample lower bound with explicit constants.

Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-.summary: Places the existential theory of the reals inside the counting hierarchy, a significant improvement over PSPACE.

Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-o.summary: Deterministic polynomial-time factorization of polynomials over prime fields without assuming GRH, a classic open problem in computer algebra.

uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-lim.summary: Resolves the "uniform bound" part of Hilbert's 16th problem: a planar polynomial vector field of degree n has at most H(n) isolated periodic orbits (limit cycles). This is one of Hilbert's 1900 problems.

two-limit-cycles-for-quintic-lienard-sys.summary: Shows quintic Liénard oscillators have at most two limit cycles, proving the degree-five case of the Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh conjecture.

A-smooth-three-torus-diffeomorphism-with.summary: Builds a smooth volume-preserving map of the 3-torus with simple Lebesgue spectrum, answering a smooth-dynamics version of a question attributed to Banach.

Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one.summary: Proves Rokhlin's 1949 multiple-mixing problem: any transformation that mixes pairs of sets automatically mixes any finite number of sets.

Positive-Metric-Entropy-for-the-Standard.summary: Proves the Chirikov standard map (a model of chaos in physics) has positive entropy for all large parameters, settling Sinai's conjecture on chaos in this famous family.

Continuous-Phase-Foliations-Create-Analy.summary: Shows continuous invariant curves near the boundary of a billiard table force an analytic collar of caustics, half of the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture.

Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Cont.summary: Proves a billiard table foliated by caustics near its boundary must be an ellipse (near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture).

The-entropy-rate-dimension-formula-for-s.summary: Proves the dimension of any self-similar measure on the line is given by the natural entropy/Lyapunov formula, even with overlaps (entropy-rate dimension conjecture).

Uniform-Permanence-in-Weakly-Reversible-.summary: Proves the permanence conjecture: in weakly reversible chemical reaction networks, all concentrations eventually stay within fixed positive bounds.

Boundedness-and-persistence-of-weakly-re.summary: Proves boundedness and persistence for weakly reversible mass-action systems: no chemical species ever goes extinct or blows up.

Weak-mixing-of-triangular-billiards-with.summary: Proves billiards in any triangle with an angle not a rational multiple of π are weakly mixing, a strong form of randomness.

Ergodicity-of-triangular-billiards-with-.summary: Proves billiards in every triangle with an angle irrational relative to π are ergodic, a long-standing open problem (previously known only for generic triangles).

A-C1-Counterexample-to-the-Entropy-Conje.summary: A C¹ map with zero entropy but exponential homological growth, disproving the C¹ self-map form of Shub's entropy conjecture.

A-finite-entropy-system-without-a-smooth.summary: A zero-entropy ergodic system that cannot be realized as a smooth volume-preserving map on any compact manifold.

Arithmetic-classification-and-non-Pisot-.summary: Classifies which Bernoulli convolutions are singular by an arithmetic criterion, and finds singular examples beyond Pisot numbers (a famous question since Erdős).

Pointwise-Multiple-Ergodic-Averages-for-.summary: Proves pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages of all lengths for mixing systems, a major case of Furstenberg's question.

Pointwise-convergence-of-fourfold-ergodi.summary: Shows averages of f(Tⁿx)g(T²ⁿx)h(T³ⁿx)k(T⁴ⁿx) converge at almost every point for mixing systems.

Triple-ergodic-averages-with-distinct-in.summary: Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages with arbitrary distinct slopes for mixing transformations.

Pointwise-convergence-of-triple-ergodic-.summary: Shows triple averages along n, 2n, 3n converge at almost every point for mixing systems, a case of Furstenberg's pointwise question.

A-translational-tile-with-no-fully-perio.summary: A single tile in 3D that tiles space only non-periodically, disproving the periodic tiling conjecture in the lowest possible dimension.

A-nine-dimensional-counterexample-to-Bor.summary: Disproves Borsuk's conjecture in dimension 9 (previously the smallest known counterexample was in dimension 64).

A-counterexample-to-Hadwigers-conjecture.summary: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture (1943), one of the most famous problems in graph theory, which predicted that graphs needing many colors must contain a large clique minor.

A-counterexample-to-the-Colin-de-Verdier.summary: Disproves the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture with graphs of independence number 2.

A-linear-list-coloring-bound-in-terms-of.summary: Proves list chromatic number is at most linear in the Hadwiger number, the "linear Hadwiger" conjecture for list coloring.

The-Euclidean-plane-is-not-five-colorabl.summary: Proves the plane cannot be colored with 5 colors without two points at distance 1 sharing a color, so its chromatic number is 6 or 7.

Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Pr.summary: Proves Erdős's famous conjecture: any set of integers whose reciprocals diverge contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions (which would include the primes, via Green–Tao).

Quantitative-Superexponential-Bounds-for.summary: Shows the van der Waerden numbers (how long a colored sequence must be to force a single-colored progression) grow faster than any exponential, answering Erdős.

A-counterexample-to-Sidorenkos-conjectur.summary: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a specific 35-vertex bipartite graph, a central conjecture in extremal graph theory.

Balanced-Counterexamples-to-Rysers-Conje.summary: Builds intersecting hypergraphs needing more cover vertices than Ryser predicted, disproving his covering conjecture at prime orders.

A-Counterexample-to-Rysers-Covering-Conj.summary: Another family of counterexamples to Ryser's covering conjecture, using prime-power constructions.

Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-i.summary: Proves Hindman's conjecture: any finite coloring of the integers contains arbitrarily large sets whose sums and products all share a color.

The-crossing-number-of-complete-graphs-S.summary: Proves the Harary–Hill conjecture giving the exact crossing number of the complete graph Kn.

The-crossing-number-of-complete-bipartit.summary: Proves Zarankiewicz's conjecture (Turán's brickyard problem) giving the exact crossing number of complete bipartite graphs.

The-higher-dimensional-Erdos-distinct-di.summary: Proves the higher-dimensional Erdős distinct distances conjecture: n points in R^d determine at least c·n^{2/d} distances.

The-weak-pinned-planar-distance-theorem-.summary: Proves almost every point of a planar set sees nearly n distinct distances (weak pinned distances conjecture).

A-power-saving-for-planar-unit-distances.summary: First power-saving improvement on the Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter n^{4/3} bound for the Erdős unit distance problem, stuck since 1984.

Combinatorial-Invariance-of-Kazhdan-Lusz.summary: Proves the combinatorial invariance conjecture: Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials depend only on the Bruhat interval's order structure.

Elementary-Positivity-of-Chromatic-Quasi.summary: Proves e-positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions (Shareshian–Wachs), generalizing the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture.

The-Sharp-Logarithmic-Exponent-of-r-5-t-.summary: Pins down the logarithmic factor in r(5,t): how large a network must be to force 5 mutual friends or t mutual strangers.

Sharp-Logarithmic-Exponents-for-Fixed-Of.summary: Pins down the logarithmic factor in the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers r(s,t) for every fixed s ≥ 6.

The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-o.summary: Proves the Burr–Erdős conjecture: the Ramsey number of the n-cube is linear in its number of vertices.

A-classification-of-finite-Euclidean-Ram.summary: Classifies which finite point configurations are Euclidean Ramsey, disproving the Leader–Russell–Walters conjecture.

A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-.summary: Proves Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture: every oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many second as first out-neighbours.

The-strong-thin-tree-conjecture-Septembe.summary: Proves the strong thin tree conjecture, a key ingredient for approximating the asymmetric traveling salesman problem.

A-polynomial-time-construction-of-strong.summary: Gives a polynomial-time algorithm to find strong thin trees, which are useful for approximating the traveling salesman problem.

Graph-Decompositions-at-the-Integral-Exp.summary: Proves the Ascoli–He–Park–Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture about random graph thresholds.

Integral-and-fractional-expectation-thre.summary: Proves Talagrand's conjecture that integral and fractional expectation thresholds agree up to a constant.

Talagrands-discrete-convexity-conjecture.summary: Proves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture, a structural statement about families of sets with high probability.

The-second-Kahn-Kalai-conjecture-Septemb.summary: Proves the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture on subgraph appearance thresholds in random graphs.

Bounded-degree-coboundary-expanders-in-e.summary: Constructs sparse high-dimensional "expanders" (simplicial complexes that are robustly connected in every degree), relevant to codes and property testing.

Deterministic-nonbipartite-Ramanujan-gra.summary: Deterministic construction of nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree and sufficiently large size.

A-uniform-influence-bound-for-hypergraph.summary: Shows symmetric properties of random hypergraphs flip from unlikely to likely in a narrow window.

A-Sharp-Threshold-Bound-for-Monotone-Gra.summary: Proves the Friedgut–Kalai conjecture: monotone graph properties have threshold width O(1/log² n).

The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Trian.summary: Determines the exact number of edges left at the end of the random triangle removal process.

Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25.summary: Determines exactly how large a two-colored complete graph must be to force a red m-cycle or a blue n-clique.

Polynomial-removal-fails-for-ordered-bin.summary: Shows a classic removal phenomenon fails for ordered binary matrices: having few copies of a pattern doesn't mean you're close to having none.

A-power-improvement-in-the-Heilbronn-tri.summary: Shows points can be placed so the smallest triangle is larger than n^{-2+c}, disproving the conjectured upper bound in Heilbronn's problem.

Positivity-of-Serres-Intersection-Multip.summary: Proves Serre's positivity conjecture for intersection multiplicities in ramified mixed characteristic, open since 1958.

Lechs-multiplicity-conjecture-September-.summary: Proves Lech's 1960 conjecture: a ring's multiplicity (a measure of how singular it is) cannot decrease along a flat extension.

A-Complete-Local-Domain-Without-a-Small-.summary: Builds a ring with no small maximal Cohen–Macaulay module, disproving Hochster's small Cohen–Macaulay conjecture for domains.

A-Torsion-Free-Group-Algebra-with-Zero-D.summary: Disproves Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture: a torsion-free group algebra can have two nonzero elements multiplying to zero.

A-Torsion-Free-Group-Algebra-That-Is-Not.summary: A torsion-free group whose group algebra over F₂ is not directly finite, disproving Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture even without torsion.

A-Counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-Direct-Fi.summary: Disproves Kaplansky's direct finiteness and Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture; the group is nonsofic.

A-Counterexample-to-the-Group-Ring-Deter.summary: Disproves the Determinant Conjecture for group rings, which was used to verify many L²-invariant results.

A-Counterexample-to-Kaplanskys-Direct-Fi.summary: Another counterexample to Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture, now in odd characteristic.

An-algebra-of-infinite-little-finitistic.summary: Builds a finite-dimensional algebra whose modules have unbounded finite projective dimension, disproving the little finitistic dimension conjecture.

An-explicit-counterexample-to-the-Auslan.summary: Disproves the Auslander–Reiten conjecture, a central conjecture in the representation theory of finite-dimensional algebras.

A-counterexample-to-Tachikawas-second-co.summary: Disproves Tachikawa's second conjecture and, with it, the Nakayama conjecture, both long-standing in representation theory of algebras.

The-Artinian-Lex-Plus-Powers-Betti-Theor.summary: Proves the Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures: ideals containing a regular sequence have the same growth as a simple model ideal, with at least as many relations.

The-Blockwise-Alperin-Weight-Conjecture-.summary: Proves Alperin's weight conjecture: the number of "modular" irreducible representations in a block of a finite group equals a count of local data called weights. A central conjecture in group representation theory since 1986.

Donovans-Conjecture-over-Algebraic-Closu.summary: Proves Donovan's conjecture: once the size of the defect group is bounded, blocks of finite groups come in only finitely many essentially different types.

Integral-Donovan-Finiteness-over-Witt-Ve.summary: Integral (Witt-vector) version of Donovan finiteness for blocks of finite groups with bounded defect.

Tensor-Saturation-for-Even-Spin-Groups-S.summary: Proves the saturation conjecture for even spin groups: if a scaled-up tensor product has an invariant, so does the original.

Universal-Tensor-Squares-for-Symmetric-G.summary: Shows almost every symmetric group has an irreducible representation whose tensor square contains all irreducibles (tensor square conjecture).

A-Cyclic-Polytabloid-Proof-of-Saxls-Conj.summary: Proves Saxl's conjecture: the tensor square of the staircase representation of the symmetric group contains every irreducible representation.

Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterizat.summary: Characterizes which finite lattices are congruence lattices of finite algebras, and shows this is undecidable.

A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattic.summary: Solves the finite lattice representation problem negatively: some finite lattice is not the congruence lattice of any finite algebra. Open since the 1960s.

The-l1-Bass-Conjecture-for-Discrete-Grou.summary: Proves the ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for all discrete groups, about traces of idempotent matrices over group algebras.

The-Bass-trace-conjecture-for-complex-gr.summary: Proves the Bass trace conjecture and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture in characteristic zero: group rings of torsion-free groups have no nontrivial idempotents.

Fiber-functors-for-finite-symmetric-tens.summary: Proves every finite symmetric tensor category in characteristic p embeds into a higher Verlinde category (Benson–Etingof–Ostrik), a "Deligne theorem" for positive characteristic.

An-Integral-Counterexample-to-Gerstens-C.summary: A ring whose K₅ class vanishes over its fraction field, disproving Gersten's conjecture in its integral form.

An-Integral-Degree-Three-Gersten-Counter.summary: A second counterexample to the integral Gersten conjecture in algebraic K-theory, in degree three.

Foulkes-Conjecture-for-the-Sixth-Symmetr.summary: Proves the sixth case of Foulkes' conjecture, comparing nested symmetric powers of a vector space.

Quadratic-Stabilization-of-the-Canonical.summary: Proves the Foulkes–Howe map is surjective once b ≥ a(a−1), a quadratic stabilization bound.

Random-Walks-on-Critical-FK-Ising-Maps-a.summary: Shows random walks on random planar maps decorated by the Ising model converge to a "Brownian motion on random surfaces" (Liouville Brownian motion).

A-Linear-Clock-for-Random-Walk-on-Tree-W.summary: Random walk on spanning-tree-weighted planar maps converges to Liouville Brownian motion, with a linear time change.

Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritica.summary: FK planar maps converge to Liouville quantum gravity spheres decorated by conformal loop ensembles, in their natural conformal embedding.

The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-an.summary: Constructs the critical Liouville quantum gravity sphere and shows FK random planar maps at q=4 converge to it.

Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-.summary: Proves Gwynne–Miller's conjecture: FK and spanning-tree planar maps converge as metric spaces to Liouville quantum gravity.

Brownian-continuum-random-tree-limits-of.summary: Shows random planar maps with FK weight q > 4 look like a random tree (Brownian continuum random tree) at large scales.

No-bigeodesics-in-planar-first-passage-p.summary: Proves planar first-passage percolation has no bi-infinite geodesics, a famous conjecture of Furstenberg/Kesten-era origin.

Strict-convexity-and-differentiability-o.summary: The exponential first-passage limit shape in 2D is strictly convex and smooth, resolving longstanding conjectures.

Critical-bond-and-site-percolation-on-th.summary: Proves there is no infinite cluster at criticality for percolation on Z³, one of the most famous open problems in probability.

No-percolation-at-criticality-on-quasi-t.summary: Proves the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture: no infinite cluster at criticality on any quasi-transitive graph.

Nonuniqueness-of-percolation-on-nonamena.summary: Proves the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture p_c < p_u on nonamenable graphs: there is a phase with infinitely many infinite clusters.

The-canonical-massive-continuum-limit-of.summary: Constructs the continuum limit of the 2D O(3) sigma model with a mass gap, a famous open problem in mathematical physics akin to Yang–Mills in spirit.

An-Isolated-Particle-Pole-for-the-Two-Di.summary: Proves the O(3) continuum field has an isolated particle pole: a genuine lowest-mass particle.

Exact-mass-asymptotics-for-the-two-dimen.summary: Computes the exact low-temperature mass gap asymptotics for the 2D O(4) model, matching physics predictions.

Sharp-mass-bounds-for-the-two-dimensiona.summary: Sharp upper and lower bounds on the mass gap (energy of the lightest particle) of the 2D O(4) spin model.

The-critical-logarithmic-correction-for-.summary: Proves the logarithmic correction in critical correlations of the 2D XY model, a subtle prediction of Kosterlitz–Thouless theory.

Critical-Center-Magnetization-in-the-Pla.summary: Conditionally computes the magnetization at the center of a box in the critical XY model.

The-Critical-Spin-Field-of-the-Planar-XY.summary: The critical XY spin field converges to the imaginary exponential of a Gaussian free field.

Essential-Singularity-of-the-Correlation.summary: Proves the Kosterlitz–Thouless essential singularity of the correlation length in the XY model (Nobel Prize physics prediction).

The-critical-correlation-exponent-of-the.summary: Proves the BKT prediction that spin correlations in the critical XY model decay like distance^{-1/4}.

BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-s.summary: Gaussian scaling limits for discrete height models throughout the rough phase, with the universal temperature 8π.

Uniform-marked-polygon-estimates-and-sha.summary: Uniform estimates for marked self-avoiding polygons and bridge moments.

Routing-densities-and-representation-con.summary: Another proof of optimal Thorp shuffle mixing, via routing densities.

Row-column-symmetry-and-contraction-of-c.summary: Another proof of optimal Thorp shuffle mixing, via row–column symmetry.

The-sharp-singularity-rate-for-biased-sy.summary: The exact exponential rate at which a random symmetric ±1 matrix with biased signs is singular.

A-CH-Obstruction-to-a-Prescribed-Categor.summary: Under the continuum hypothesis, shows a proposed threshold for categoricity transfer in model theory is not enough.

Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Eleme.summary: Proves Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC: if a class of structures has a unique model in one large size, it has a unique model in all large sizes. A central problem in model theory.

Rigidity-of-the-Turing-degrees-September.summary: Proves the Turing degrees are rigid: there is no nontrivial symmetry of the ordering of "how uncomputable" problems are. A long-standing question in computability theory.

Single-fold-Diophantine-representations-.summary: Every computably enumerable set has a Diophantine description with unique solutions (single-fold conjecture), strengthening the solution of Hilbert's tenth problem.

Choiceless-polynomial-time-with-counting.summary: Shows choiceless polynomial time with counting does not capture all polynomial-time properties, confirming the Blass–Gurevich–Shelah conjecture.

Weak-and-strong-normalization-in-pure-ty.summary: Proves the Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture: in pure type systems, if every term can be evaluated then every evaluation terminates.

Parabolic-intersections-in-Artin-groups-.summary: Shows that intersecting any collection of "parabolic" subgroups of an Artin group gives another parabolic subgroup, a basic structural fact long conjectured.

Nonsingular-systems-of-equations-over-ar.summary: Proves Howie's conjecture: systems of equations over any group can be solved in a larger group whenever their exponent pattern is nondegenerate.

The-Kervaire-Theorem-for-Groups-Septembe.summary: Proves the Kervaire conjecture: adding one generator and one relation can never kill a nontrivial group.

A-hyperbolic-group-with-no-geometric-CAT.summary: Constructs a hyperbolic group that cannot act geometrically on any nonpositively curved (CAT(0)) space, answering a well-known question of Gromov.

Baumslag-Solitar-free-one-relator-groups.summary: Proves Gersten's conjecture: one-relator groups without Baumslag–Solitar subgroups are hyperbolic.
